reassessment_reason: Surface all-registered versus active-only scope ambiguity and distinguish 2026 residential-address suppression from CMRA disclosure requirements.

access.bulk: INBiz advertises a month-start full file through prior month-end, with 12 months of update eligibility. Regulatory analysis describes USB baseline delivery, $8,000 one-time or $9,500 plus $500 per selected monthly update.
access.api: Monthly download access does not establish an unattended API.
access.search: INBiz requires an account to purchase bulk files; no login, purchase, sample download or entity search occurred.

fields.summary: Exact bulk schema, Business-ID lifecycle, control totals and person-free projection remain unverified. The $35 new-business list is a separate product, not a full registry.

active_status_semantics: Biennial reporting maintains registry status; general partnerships and sole proprietors do not register. Operational activity cannot be inferred from registry standing.
statewide_completeness: Product narrative says all registered businesses; regulatory analysis comparison table says all active. Resolve this scope ambiguity before assigning a denominator.
address_zip: 2026 guidance permits eligible remote businesses to exclude a residential address and separately requires CMRA disclosures. It does not say CMRA addresses are categorically withheld. Keep ZIP5/ZIP4 separate and suppressed addresses unknown.
automation_terms_fees: Account, payment, delivery and automation terms need verification. The March 2025 first-public-comment document is proposed-rule evidence, not proof of final adoption.
redistribution: Commercial demand for bulk records does not itself settle retention, geocoding, derived publication or redistribution terms.
temporal_refresh: Updates are described as differential. Tombstones, ordering, correction/replay, baseline compatibility and checksums remain unresolved.

citations.evidence: Account requirement, all-registered month-end snapshot and optional monthly updates.
USB baseline and price descriptions; page 6 comparison labels Indiana one-time coverage all active, unlike the page 2 narrative.
Biennial reports and exclusion of general partnerships and sole proprietors.
2026 remote-residential suppression and distinct CMRA disclosure requirements.
First-public-comment notice with proposed bulk fee provisions; not used as proof of final rule adoption.

strongest_next_action: Prepare a document-only clarification of all-registered versus active scope, current USB/download delivery, redaction flags, person-free schema, differential replay and intended-use terms. HOLD remains; no account, purchase, contact or acquisition is authorized.
